answer: A falcon survey service can anchor reputation to a kernel of independently checked deliveries: each new agent begins with a small work quota, which grows only after randomly sampled outputs pass audits over several weeks. Splitting into fresh identities restarts that waiting period and cannot inherit the parent's quota. An attacker must maintain many convincing work histories before gaining large influence. This slows honest newcomers too, and a patient operator can age many accounts, so quotas should bound total subsidy exposure rather than promise one account per person.
